# PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005] Contents of this Part

## I APPLICATION OF THIS PART

## Scope and interpretation

## 76.1

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.1] (1) This Part contains rules about–

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.1] (a) control order proceedings in the High Court; and

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.1] (b) appeals to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in such proceedings. [PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.1] (2) In the case of proceedings brought by virtue of section 11(2) of the Act, the rules in this Part shall apply with any modification which the court considers necessary. [PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.1] (3) In this Part –

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.1] (a) ‘the Act’ means the Prevention of Terrorism Act 2005;

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.1] (b) ‘closed material’ means any relevant material that the Secretary of State objects to disclosing to a relevant party;

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.1] (c) ‘control order proceedings’ has the same meaning as in section 11(6) of the Act;

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.1] (d) ‘controlled person’, has the same meaning as in section 15(1) of the Act;

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.1] (e) ‘legal representative’ is to be construed in accordance with paragraph 11 of the Schedule to the Act;

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.1] (f) ‘open material’ means any relevant material that the Secretary of State does not object to disclosing to a relevant party;

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.1] (h) ‘relevant material’ has the same meaning as in paragraph 4(5) of the Schedule to the Act;

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.1] (i) ‘relevant party’ has the same meaning as in paragraph 11 of the Schedule to the Act;

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.1] (j) ‘special advocate’ means a person appointed under paragraph 7 of the Schedule to the Act. [PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.1] (4) For the purposes of this Part, disclosure is contrary to the public interest if it is made contrary to the interests of national security, the international relations of the United Kingdom, the detection and prevention of crime, or in any other circumstances where disclosure is likely to harm the public interest. ## Modification to the overriding objective

## 76.2

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.2] (1) Where this Part applies, the overriding objective in Part 1, and so far as relevant any other rule, must be read and given effect in a way which is compatible with the duty set out in paragraph (2). [PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.2] (2) The court must ensure that information is not disclosed contrary to the public interest. [PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.2] (3) Subject to paragraph (2), the court must satisfy itself that the material available to it enables it properly to determine proceedings. ## II APPLICATION TO THE HIGH COURT RELATING TO DEROGATING CONTROL ORDERS

## Scope of this section

## 76.3

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.3] (1) This section of this Part contains rules about applications relating to derogating control orders. [PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.3] (2) Part 23 does not apply to an application made under this section of this Part. ## Applications for the making of a derogating control order

## 76.4

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.4] An application for the making of a derogating control order under section 4(1) of the Act must be made by the Secretary of State by filing with the court –

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.4] (a) a statement of reasons to support the application for –

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.4] (i) making such an order, and

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.4] (ii) imposing each of the obligations to be imposed by that order;

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.4] (b) all relevant material;

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.4] (c) any written submissions; and

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.4] (d) a draft of the order sought. ## Directions for a full hearing on notice

## 76.5

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.5] (1) When the court makes a derogating control order under section 4(3) of the Act it must –

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.5] (a) immediately fix a date, time and place for a further hearing at which the controlled person, his legal representative and a special advocate (if one has been appointed) can be present; and

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.5] (b) unless the court otherwise directs, that date must be no later than 7 days from the date that the order is made. [PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.5] (2) At the hearing referred to in paragraph (1)(a) the court must give directions –

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.5] (a) for the holding of a full hearing under section 4(1)(b) of the Act to determine whether to confirm the control order (with or without modifications) or to revoke it; and

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.5] (b) specifying the date and time by which the parties and special advocate must file and serve any written evidence or written submissions in accordance with rule 76.30. [PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.5] (3) When giving directions under paragraph (2), the court must have regard to the need to expedite the full hearing. ## Applications on notice

## 76.6

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.6] (1) An application under section 4(9) for the renewal, or under section 7(4) of the Act, for the revocation of a control order or for the modification of obligations imposed by such an order, must be made in accordance with this rule. [PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.6] (2) An application by the Secretary of State must be made by –

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.6] (a) filing with the court–

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.6] (i) a statement of reasons to support the application,

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.6] (ii) all relevant material,

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.6] (iii) any written submissions, and

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.6] (iv) a draft of the order sought; and

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.6] (b) serving on the controlled person or his legal representative any open material. [PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.6] (3) An application by the controlled person must be made by filing with the court and serving on the Secretary of State –

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.6] (a) a statement of reasons to support the application;

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.6] (b) any written evidence upon which he relies;

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.6] (c) any written submissions; and

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.6] (d) where appropriate, a draft of the order sought. [PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.6] (4) If the controlled person wishes to oppose an application made under this rule, he must as soon as practicable file with the court, and serve on the Secretary of State, any written evidence and any written submissions upon which he relies. [PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.6] (5) If the Secretary of State wishes to oppose an application made under this rule, he must as soon as practicable–

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.6] (a) file with the court–

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.6] (i) all relevant material, and

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.6] (ii) any written submissions; and

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.6] (b) serve on the controlled person any open material. [PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.6] (Attention is drawn to rule 76.18 relating to the address for issuing proceedings in the High Court. Rules 76.28 and 76.29 will apply where any closed material is filed by the Secretary of State). ## Scope of this section

## 76.7

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.7] This section of this Part contains rules about –

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.7] (a) applications under section 3(1)(a) of the Act (application for permission to make a non-derogating control order);

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.7] (b) references under section 3(3) of the Act (reference of a non-derogating control order made without permission); and

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.7] (c) appeals to the High Court under section 10 of the Act (appeals relating to non-derogating control orders). ## Application for permission to make non-derogating control order

## 76.8

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.8] An application under section 3(1)(a) for permission to make a non-derogating control order must be made by the Secretary of State by filing with the court –

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.8] (a) a statement of reasons to support the application;

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.8] (b) all relevant material;

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.8] (c) any written submissions; and

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.8] (d) the proposed control order. ## References under section 3(3) of the Act

## 76.9

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.9] (1) This rule applies where the Secretary of State makes a reference under section 3(3) of the Act (reference of a non-derogating control order). [PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.9] (2) The Secretary of State must promptly file with the court –

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.9] (a) a statement of the reasons for –

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.9] (i) making the control order,

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.9] (ii) imposing the obligations imposed by that order;

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.9] (b) all relevant material; and

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.9] (c) any written submissions. ## Directions for hearing on application for permission or on a reference

## 76.10

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.10] (1) This rule applies where the court gives directions under section 3(2)(c) or (6)(b) or (c) of the Act. [PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.10] (2) The court must immediately–

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.10] (a) fix a date, time and place for a further hearing at which the controlled person, his legal representative and a special advocate (if one has been appointed) can be present; and

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.10] (b) unless the court otherwise directs –

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.10] (i) in the case of directions given under section 3(2)(c), that date must be no later than 7 days from the date on which the notice of the terms of the control order is delivered to the controlled person in accordance with section 7(8) of the Act; or

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.10] (ii) in the case of directions given under section 3(6)(b) or (c), that date must be 7 days from the date on which the court’s determination on the reference is made. [PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.10] (3) At the hearing referred to in paragraph (2), the court must give directions –

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.10] (a) for a hearing under section 3(10); and

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.10] (b) specifying the date and time by which the parties and special advocate must file and serve any written evidence or written submissions in accordance with rule 76.30. [PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.10] (4) When giving directions under paragraph (3), the court must have regard to the need to expedite that hearing. [PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.10] (Rules 76.28 and 76.29 will apply where any closed material is filed by the Secretary of State). ## Appeals under section 10 of the Act

## 76.11

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.11] This rule and rules 76.12 to 76.15 apply to an appeal under section 10 of the Act (appeals relating to a non-derogating control order). ## Modification of Part 52 (appeals)

## 76.12

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.12] (1) Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal under section 10 of the Act, subject to –

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.12] (a) rule 76.2;

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.12] (b) the rules in section 5 of this Part; and

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.12] (c) the modifications set out in paragraphs (2) and (3) of this rule. [PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.12] (2) The following rules do not apply to appeals under section 10 of the Act –

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.12] (a) rule 52.12 (permission);

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.12] (b) rule 52.12 (appellant’s notice);

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.12] (c) rule 52.13 (respondent’s notice); and

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.12] (d) rule 52.21 (hearing of appeals). [PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.12] (3) Rule 52.2 (all parties to comply with Practice Directions 52A to 52E apply, but the parties shall not be required to comply with paragraphs 5.1 to 5.3 of Practice Direction 52A and paragraphs 6.3 to 6.6 of Practice Direction 52B. ## Notice of appeal

## 76.13

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.13] (1) The controlled person must give notice of appeal by –

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.13] (a) filing it with the court; and

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.13] (b) serving a copy of the notice and any accompanying documents on the Secretary of State. [PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.13] (2) The notice of appeal must–

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.13] (a) set out the grounds of the appeal; and

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.13] (b) state the name and address of–

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.13] (i) the controlled person, and

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.13] (ii) any legal representative of that person. [PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.13] (3) A notice of appeal may include an application for an order under rule 76.19 requiring anonymity. [PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.13] (4) The notice of appeal must be filed with –

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.13] (a) a copy of the order that is the subject of the appeal;

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.13] (b) a copy of the Secretary of State’s decision on an application for the revocation of the control order, or for the modification of an obligation imposed by such an order. [PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.13] (Attention is drawn to rule 76.18 relating to the address for issuing proceedings in the High Court). ## Time limit for appealing

## 76.14

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.14] (1) Subject to paragraph (2), the controlled person must give notice of appeal no later than 28 days after receiving –

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.14] (a) the notice setting out the terms of the order, renewal or modification that is the subject of the appeal; or

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.14] (b) notice of the decision by the Secretary of State on an application for the revocation of the control order, or for the modification of an obligation imposed by such an order. [PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.14] (2) In a case where the Secretary of State has failed to determine an application for the revocation of the control order, or for the modification of an obligation imposed by such an order, the controlled person must file the notice of appeal –

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.14] (a) no earlier than 28 days; and

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.14] (b) no later than 42 days;

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.14] after the date the application was made. ## Secretary of State’s reply

## 76.15

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.15] (1) If the Secretary of State wishes to oppose an appeal made under section 10 of the Act, he must no later than 14 days after he is served with the notice of appeal –

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.15] (a) file with the court–

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.15] (i) all relevant material, and

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.15] (ii) any written submissions; and

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.15] (b) serve on the controlled person any open material. ## IV APPEALS TO THE COURT OF APPEAL

## Modification of Part 52 (appeals)

## 76.16

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.16] (1) Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in control order proceedings, subject to –

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.16] (a) rule 76.2;

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.16] (b) the rules in section 5 of this Part; and

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.16] (c) paragraphs (2) and (3) of this rule. [PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.16] (2) The following rules do not apply to appeals to the Court of Appeal –

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.16] (a) rule 52.12 (appellant’s notice); and

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.16] (b) rule 52.13 (respondent’s notice); but

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.16] the provisions of rules 76.13 and 76.15 shall apply with appropriate modifications. [PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.16] (3) Rule 52.2 (all parties to comply with Practice Directions 52A to 52E apply, but the parties shall not be required to comply with paragraphs 6.3 to 6.6 of Practice Direction 52B and paragraph 28 of Practice Direction 52C. ## V GENERAL PROVISIONS

## Scope of this section

## 76.17

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.17] This section of this Part applies to –

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.17] (a) control order proceedings in the High Court; and

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.17] (b) appeals to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in such proceedings. ## Address for issuing proceedings in the High Court

## 76.18

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.18] Any control order proceedings must be issued at the Administrative Court Office, Room C315, Royal Courts of Justice, Strand, London, WC2A 2LL. ## Applications for anonymity

## 76.19

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.19] (1) The controlled person or the Secretary of State may apply for an order requiring the anonymity of the controlled person. [PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.19] (2) An application under paragraph (1) may be made at any time, irrespective of whether any control order proceedings have been commenced. [PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.19] (3) An application may be made without notice to the other party. [PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.19] (4) References in this rule –

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.19] (a) to an order requiring anonymity for the controlled person are to be construed in accordance with paragraph 5(3) of the Schedule to the Act; and

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.19] (b) to the controlled person, in relation to a time before the control order has been made, are to be construed in accordance with paragraph 5(4) of the Schedule to the Act. ## Notification of hearing

## 76.20

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.20] Unless the court orders otherwise, it must serve notice of the date, time and place fixed for any hearing on–

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.20] (a) every party, whether or not entitled to attend that hearing; and

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.20] (b) if one has been appointed for the purposes of the hearing, the special advocate or those instructing him. ## Hearings

## 76.21

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.21] (1) The following proceedings must be determined at a hearing –

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.21] (a) a hearing pursuant to directions given under section 4(1)(b) of the Act (derogating control orders);

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.21] (b) a hearing pursuant to directions given under sections 3(2)(c) or (6)(b) or (c) of the Act (non-derogating control orders);

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.21] (c) an appeal under section 10 of the Act (appeal relating to a non-derogating control order);

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.21] (d) an appeal to the Court of Appeal from an order of the High Court made in any of the above proceedings; and

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.21] (e) a hearing under rule 76.29(2) (consideration of Secretary of State’s objection). [PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.21] (2) Paragraph (1)(c) and (d) do not apply where –

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.21] (a) the appeal is withdrawn by the controlled person;

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.21] (b) the Secretary of State consents to the appeal being allowed; or

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.21] (c) the controlled person is outside the United Kingdom or it is impracticable to give him notice of a hearing and, in either case, he is unrepresented. ## Hearings in private

## 76.22

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.22] (1) If the court considers it necessary for any relevant party and his legal representative to be excluded from a hearing or part of a hearing in order to secure that information is not disclosed contrary to the public interest, it must –

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.22] (a) direct accordingly; and

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.22] (b) conduct the hearing, or that part of it from which the relevant party and his legal representative are excluded, in private. [PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.22] (2) The court may conduct a hearing or part of a hearing in private for any other good reason.
